- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or volatile.  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns positive or stabilizes after a downturn.  
- Lag in correction: model often overshoots early in the forecast horizon, then gradually converges — adjust for 3–5 day lag in mean reversion.  
- High sentiment volatility (e.g., alternating +/–0.40) correlates with overconfidence in short-term forecasts — reduce forecast amplitude by 5–10% in such cases.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model tends to overreact — apply downward bias correction of 2–5% for the next 5 days.  
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs — if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, cap forecast peak at 1.5x recent high unless sentiment turns bullish.
